scope: Script-only hardening and read-only validation of the owned cp46 rollback guard. No rollback execution, tunnel restart, binary rebuild, or product/runtime mutation.

admission.authority: cp46c conditional admission after cp36h STOP, TODO authorityGO77
admission.baseline: cp46b and root-cp46b receipt; root confirmed all seven owned container identities/images/services/project/owner/running and five volumes. The cp46 original evidence contains one shortened volume ID; cp46b/root readback is authoritative for that identity.

changes: Hard-codes the exact cp46 owner/child PIDs, UTC creation timestamps, parent, executable paths, executable SHA256s, complete child argv, target, and empty-config hash; callers cannot supply alternate identities.
Acquires and retains .NET Process handles for both exact processes, checks full StartTime UTC ticks, CIM metadata, hashes, state metadata, and rechecks the same handles before any permitted action.
Provides explicit -ValidateOnly mode; a separate -ExecuteRollback switch is required to reach the pinned-child Kill branch.
Fails closed on missing/mismatching process, timestamps, ancestry, command line, target, binary/config hashes, or state. Rollback branch targets only the pinned child handle.

liveNativeIdentity.timePrecision: Get-Process.StartTime UTC ticks matched the immutable cp46 timestamps at 100 ns precision. Win32_Process.CreationDate on this host is truncated to microseconds; the script independently compares that value to the exact timestamp truncated to 1 microsecond. No broad time tolerance is used.

negativeControl.interpretation: Deliberately wrong expected child creation ticks fail closed.

guardValidation.processHandleRecheck: both original handles remained alive and retained exact StartTime ticks after metadata/hash/state checks

initialCheckCorrections: The first parser invocation did not receive its Windows path through the WSL-to-Windows environment bridge; this was an invocation-path issue, not a PowerShell syntax result. The parser was rerun with an explicit literal path and returned zero syntax errors.

The first live check exposed floating-point truncation in the CIM microsecond comparison. It failed closed without acting. The comparison was corrected to integer tick truncation; exact validation then passed.
